name: ci-preflight-full-mode-gap
title: CI never fully validates a pull request's Trellis content: full mode skips the preflight, bookkeeping mode runs it against the previous head
description: Two gaps stop CI from fully validating a pull request's Trellis content. (1) WHICH LANE: the review preflight's exact-head validation runs only under the bookkeeping classifier mode, and the classifier's first gate is the event action rather than the diff (tests.yml:137-139), so every pull request's INITIAL head is full and is never validated whatever it contains. (2) WHICH DIFF: in the lane that does run, the base is SD_AI_COMMAND_PACK_REVIEW_PREFLIGHT_BASE_REF=BEFORE_SHA (tests.yml:253), which the workflow's own comment at :157 identifies as the PR's previous pushed head, so the three checks that are both diff-scoped and able to fail -- changed task metadata, changed task topology, task context manifests -- plus the baseline-dependent half of journal validation see only the newest push. 'Fully' is load-bearing: the four repo-wide checks fire whenever the preflight runs -- which is why PR #358's documentation reference failed on its synchronize head -- and a PR whose every change lands on a successful bookkeeping successor is in fact fully covered. What is missing is the GUARANTEE: whole-PR coverage is an accident of event actions and push rhythm, not a property of the PR. Gap 2's independent residual is the cross-push case, where a later push invalidates what an earlier push committed (parent task.json naming a child that push 2 deletes) so the bad state is in no single incremental diff; it also constrains gap 1's fix, since github.event.before is not a commit on an opened event. Demonstrated on PR #358 and PR #365 for gap 1, and on commit 3d8abb41 for gap 2, where the same tree fails with base=HEAD^ and passes with base=HEAD. Four task records with an empty description reached main and none was caught by CI, though only 3d8abb41 postdates both gaps -- the three from d97244e3 predate the bookkeeping lane entirely (added b16d9e69, 2026-07-27). No post-merge net dedicated to merged content exists either: main push runs degrade to full via history_contains_merge, so nothing re-examines a commit because it landed. Merged content is caught by accident or not at all: normally by one of the four repo-wide checks, on some later unrelated head that happens to route bookkeeping -- observed on 2026-08-08, when two broken references on main surfaced on an unrelated branch -- while the three diff-scoped checks revisit it only if some later diff happens to select the same path again, which is a coincidence of what someone edits next rather than a net. Fixing only gap 1 leaves the cross-push case merging green.
creator: sdelmas
